    Infractions Classification and Application V. 26.4   2/6

1.​Definition
Authenticity rules are meant to be followed by all competitors attending Buhurt International
tournaments, no matter the category. If a competitor shows up with an armor, shield or weapon that does
not comply with the Authenticity rules, he/she risks a penalty.




                       2.​Infraction Classification
During Authenticity Check, Authenticity officers will evaluate the entire equipment of competitors before
the start of the tournament. Any violation of the Authenticity rules will result in an infraction. Infractions
can be classified under 3 different levels:


       2.1.​ Minor infraction
It is a small detail not easy to see, and it does not affect the coherence of the whole armor (small traces
of rust, hammering marks, little datation difference between 2 parts etc.).​

       2.2.​ Moderate Infraction
It is something forbidden by the Authenticity rules (i.e badly designed helmet, over numerous eye bars
etc.). Not respecting the rules can't be accepted, thus it is not severe enough to prevent the fighter from
entering the list.​

       2.3.​ Major infraction
Fantasy armor or totally inaccurate equipment, that prevent the fighter from entering the list and damage
the image of the sport, the teams and Buhurt International.​




  Infractions Classification and Application V. 26.4                                                      3/6

3.​Application of the Rules
A violation of the authenticity rules will result in a green card. Depending on the rank of tournament,
infraction will be applied differently.

A green card combined with a yellow card will result in a red card and the competitor will be disqualified
from the tournament.

A competitor can receive only 1 green card per tournament, no matter how many infractions they have.

If a competitor fixes the issue(s) that warranted a green card, the green card can be removed after
validation by the Authenticity Officer in charge of the event.

Green cards will be represented by a green ribbon worn at the competitor’s belt. It is mandatory to keep
it during the whole competition. Any removal of the green card will be considered as an attempt to cheat.

Only the Authenticity Officer in charge of the event can allow a fighter to remove the green card from
their belt.




  Infractions Classification and Application V. 26.4                                                4/6

3.1.​ Source
No authenticity check required.​
Authenticity members on site will be able to give advice and guidance.

       3.2.​ Classic
Authenticity check is mandatory prior to the start of the tournament. ​
A competitor is allowed to enter the list if they respect the following cumulative criterias:

  ●​ Have no more than 3 minors infraction (if they have 4 or more, they will receive a green card).
  ●​ Have no more than 1 moderate infraction (if they have 2 or more, they will receive a green card.
  ●​ Have no major infraction.

       3.3.​ Regional
Authenticity check is mandatory prior to the start of the tournament.
A competitor is allowed to enter the list if they respect the following cumulative criterias.
  ●​ Have no more than 2 minors infraction, if you have 3 or more, then they will receive a green card.
  ●​ Have no moderate infraction. If they have 1 or more, they will receive a green card.
  ●​ Have no major infraction.


       3.4.​ Conference
Authenticity check is mandatory prior to the start of the tournament.
A competitor is allowed to enter the list if they respect the following cumulative criterias.
  ●​ Have no more than 1 minor infraction, if you have 2 or more, then they will receive a green card.
  ●​ Have no moderate infraction.
  ●​ Have no major infraction.

Note: as an exceptional measure, for season 2025, tournaments of Conference level will be considered
as Regional regarding Authenticity rules. It means a competitor with 1 moderate infraction will be allowed
to fight, but will receive a green card.
